title: Sequence-distribution-driven bucket resizing & depad optimizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a runtime component that dynamically resizes sequence-length buckets and selectively removes padding (depad) during prefill and decode to reduce wasted tokens and enable better kernel selection. Focus is on improving p95/p99 latency and GPU utilization for mixed-length workloads without regressing single-request latency.
background: We observe large token waste caused by static bucketing and conservative padding across workloads with heavy long-tail sequence distributions (chat history + code + short queries). Existing bucket schemes group many short-prefill requests with long decodes, causing unnecessary padding and suboptimal kernel choices. Previous tickets explored length-adaptive bucketing but left gaps around prefill/decode coordination and kernel switch thresholds.
goals: Reduce effective padded tokens per second by >= 22% on mixed workloads (internal synthetic trace)
Improve tail latency (p95/p99) by 10-20% for customer scenarios with high sequence variance
Avoid >5% regression on single-request median latency
Provide deterministic fallback when depadding causes model-incompatible batch shapes
acceptance_criteria: Automated benchmark shows padded-token reduction >= 20% on mixed-seq benchmark in perf lab
No correctness regressions in generation outputs (compare token-level diffs on canonical eval prompts)
Kernel selection rules integrated into runtime and feature-flagged (off by default)
Metrics surfaced in Console: padded_tokens_saved, bucket_resizes, kernel_switches, depad_failures
End-to-end canary rollout executed for 48h with no SLO violations before broad rollout
design_summary: Introduce a lightweight online bucket-resizer that maintains short-term sequence-length histograms per route and per model variant. On each scheduling window we compute optimal bucket cutpoints using a cost function that balances token waste, expected kernel efficiency (from kernel performance model), and decode latency impact. Add a depad pass during prefill that trims trailing padding in micro-batches when safe. Coordinate with decode-time kernel selection by allowing a 'soft' kernel switch: keep prefill in kernel A (fast for long sequences) but allow decode to switch to kernel B if the depad reduces seqlen below a threshold. All changes behind runtime feature flag and governed by per-route policies.
algorithm_notes: Windowed histogram (30s, exponentially decaying) keyed by route+model_variant
Cost function: cost(bucket) = alpha * padded_tokens + beta * kernel_penalty + gamma * latency_tail_penalty
Use constrained knapsack-like greedy cutpoint search for O(k*n) runtime where k = target bucket count (default 8)
Depad heuristics: only remove padding if it is trailing and all KV cache offsets remain consistent; otherwise skip depad and emit metric depad_failures
Kernel penalty derived from offline microbenchmarks: per-kernel throughput vs seqlen curve stored as lightweight lookup table in runtime
runtime_changes: Add bucket-resizer actor to scheduler that proposes new bucket cutpoints every 30s
Expose per-route config: max_buckets, apply_threshold (minimum padded token savings to change), allow_depad boolean
Implement depad pass in prefill path that rewrites batch shapes and adjusts KV offsets; ensure memcopy costs are bounded and measured
Introduce safe kernel-switch handshake: dispatcher can request decode-stage kernel change if depad reduces sequence length below kernel B's lower bound
Add metrics and tracing spans for decision introspection
kernel_selection_rules: Prefer fused attention kernels for sequences < 512 when depad savings are significant
If depad predicted final seqlen crosses kernel boundary and saving > apply_threshold, select decode kernel accordingly
Fallback: when depad pass not applicable, keep existing kernel to avoid memcopy/regression
attention_optimizations: Enable attention fusion for short-seq batches created after depad
Apply causal-kv prefetch heuristic to reduce decode stalls for prefills with long KV chains
Add lightweight per-batch attention-sparsity check to decide whether to enable a strided/blocked attention path
Ensure attention kernel chosen supports current quantization profile and does not require re-quantization at runtime
prefill_decode_scheduling: During prefill, evaluate per-request final_length_estimate using prompt metadata and historical route profiles
If estimated final_length << allocated bucket, attempt depad and re-pack micro-batches within the scheduling window
Hold decode until depad+repack completes or a timeout (default 50ms) is reached to prevent head-of-line blocking
Allow decode to use a tighter batch window if depad reduces seqlen variance across micro-batch members
experiment_plan: Phase 1 (lab): run synthetic traces with mixed-length distribution vs baseline for 48h and gather padded token and tail latency metrics
Phase 2 (shadow traffic): enable feature flag in host staging cluster with 10% shadow traffic for customer routes identified as high-variance
Phase 3 (canary): run decode-enabled depad on 1% production traffic with full metrics and alerting
Phase 4: 48h canary expansion to 10% then full rollout if no SLO regressions
metrics_targets: kernel_switch_rate: tracked, expected 5-15% of decode batches
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged in runtime binary (off by default)
Short-lived canary (48h) with rollout checks in Console dashboard
If canary fails: auto rollback and capture decision traces for postmortem
Gradual rollout with per-region gating to minimize blast radius
risks_mitigations: Risk: memcopy overhead from depad repacking increases median latency. Mitigation: instrument memcopy cost and disable depad when memcopy latency > threshold
Risk: depad causes subtle KV misalignment leading to wrong outputs. Mitigation: strict invariants and test harness with golden token comparison; fail-open on any detected mismatch
Risk: kernel switch oscillation. Mitigation: hysteresis on kernel switch decisions and min_time_between_switches (default 5s)
Risk: increased scheduler CPU usage. Mitigation: resize histogram sampling rate and use approximate sketches if CPU pressure observed
